title: Fee Basis for Cancelled Genetic Accessions: Patient Financial Services Decision Table
content:
The fee basis of the genetic cancellation handling fee on a Laboratory Test Orders accession of the Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing class depends on how the accession is billed. For an insurance-billed accession it also depends on the payer class of its coverage with Insurance Coverage & Claims.

**Clause.** When the accession is billed self-pay and its good faith estimate amount carries an estimate date no more than **90** calendar days before today, the fee basis is **40 percent** of that quote instead of the class fee. When the accession is billed insurance and the payer class of its coverage prohibits patient billing beyond the copay, the fee basis is zero. Any other genetic accession takes the class fee as its fee basis.

| Billing method on the accession | Further condition | Fee basis |
|---|---|---|
| Self-pay | A genetic self-pay quote stands on the accession, dated no more than 90 calendar days before today | 40 percent of that quote |
| Insurance | The payer class of the coverage billed prohibits patient billing beyond the copay | zero |
| Any other case | — | the class fee |

**Boundary on the quote date (hypothetical).** A quote dated exactly 90 calendar days before today is within the period, and the fee basis is 40 percent of it. A quote dated 91 days before today is outside it, so the accession falls to the class fee.

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** A self-pay genetic accession with a quote of 349.00 dated 30 days ago has a fee basis of 40 percent of 349.00, that is 139.60.

**Points of judgement.**

- *Insurance-billed, payer class allows patient billing.* The fee basis is the class fee.
- *Self-pay, no quote on the accession.* The fee basis is the class fee.
